The following observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as Lalita Kumari Vs. Govt. of UP Writ Petition (Criminal) No.68 of 2008 has held that:
"Therefore, in view of various counter claims regarding registration or non registration, what is necessary is only that the information given to the police must disclose the commission of a cognizable offence.

entities.text: Lalita Kumari Vs. Govt. of UP Writ Petition (Criminal) No.68 of 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such a situation, registration of an FIR is mandatory.

However, if no cognizable offence is made out in the information given, then the FIR need not be registered immediately and perhaps the police can conduct a sort of preliminary verification or inquiry for the limited purpose of ascertaining as to whether a cognizable offence has been committed.
But, if the information given clearly mentions the commission of a cognizable offence, there is no other option but to register an FIR forthwith.

Other considerations are not relevant at the stage of registration of FIR, such as, whether the information is falsely given, whether the information is genuine, whether the information is credible etc.
These are the issues that have to be verified during the investigation of the FIR.
At the stage of registration of Fir, what is to seen is merely whether the information given ex facie discloses the commission of cognizable offence.

If, after investigation, the information given is found by CHANDER CHANDER Date:
MOHAN 2023.02.20  
 
CR Revision No. 18/2020 Sarabjit Singh Lamba Vs. State & Others Page no. 10 of  to be false, there is always an option to prosecute the complainant for filing a false FIR".

sentences.text: Once an information is received by the police regarding a cognizable offence (and it is also well settled that the same may be provided by even a stranger) it is duty of the police to register an FIR and take it to logical conclusion.

In the present case the information is also backed by a preliminary enquiry by the police and moreover, it has also passed the scrutiny of Ld. Magistrate who directed the registration of FIR U/s 156(3) CrPC.
Infact, it is duty of the revisionist to cooperate with the police if he thinks that he has nothing to do with the said forgery.

It is duty of the police to ensure that the affidavits are attested by genuine notaries/bear genuine stamps or signatures otherwise the very objective of affirmation of an affidavit before the notary would be lost.
It is argued by counsel for the revisionist that when an innocent person is implicated, he suffers from loss of reputation and his personal liberty is seriously impaired.
The Ld. Trial Court has already taken care of the above misgivings of the revisionist and the following extract of the impugned order is relevant.

It be seen that there is sufficient material for the arrest of accused persons.
It is not a settled law that power to arrest is different from justification to do so.
Reference may be made to (Court on its Motion Vs. CBI Volume 109 (2004) DLT page 494).

Therefore, he Digitally signed by pleaded for a fresh look at Section 154 of the Code, CHANDER CHANDER MOHAN MOHAN Date:
2023.02.20 10:44:39 +0530 CR Revision No. 18/2020 Sarabjit Singh Lamba Vs.

sentences.text: It is true that a delicate balance has to be maintained between the interest of the society and protecting the liberty of an individual.
As already discussed above, there are already sufficient safeguards provided in the Code which duly protect the liberty of an individual in case of registration of false FIR.
At the same time, Section 154 was drafted keeping in mind the interest of the victim and the society.
Therefore, we are of the cogent view that mandatory registration of FIRs under Section 154 of the Code will not be in contravention of Article 21 of the Constitution."
15. In view of the above reasons, the present revision petition is dismissed.
Needless to mention that the stay on the direction of the order of Ld. MM dt. 16.01.2020 ordering the registration of FIR stands vacated.
Police to register the FIR as per the impugned order dt. 16.01.2020 of the Ld. MM and proceed further with the matter.
